claims.text: A Pulumi blog post titled 'SST Runs on the Pulumi Engine: What It Means to Build on Pulumi' exists at /blog/sst-built-on-pulumi/ and covers the engine mechanics behind SST's migration to Pulumi.
AWS CDK tied infrastructure to AWS, and multi-cloud with CDK was nearly impossible.
SST was originally built on AWS CDK, which lets developers define infrastructure using TypeScript or Python.

AWS CDK supports only AWS, only TypeScript and Python, and uses CloudFormation state and AWS Secrets Manager only for secrets, whereas Pulumi supports AWS, Azure, GCP, on-prem and any programming language.
Pulumi deployments are faster than AWS CDK deployments because CDK relies on CloudFormation.
Ion is the code name for SST's new deployment engine using Pulumi instead of CDK/CloudFormation, and once stable it will be released as SST v3.
SST uses Pulumi behind the scenes for providers and deployment engine and bridges Terraform providers through Pulumi.
SST makes money primarily through its managed service SST Console, which is optional and includes a free tier.
Pulumi lets you define infrastructure in TypeScript, Python, Go, or C# and deploy to AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, and on-premises.
SST v3 replaced AWS CDK and CloudFormation with an embedded Pulumi engine that calls Terraform-bridged providers to make cloud API calls.
Running `sst deploy` requires no separate Pulumi install and no Pulumi account; the engine ships inside the SST CLI.
SST keeps state in an S3 bucket in the user's own AWS account, not Pulumi Cloud.
SST deploys to AWS and more than 150 other providers.
SST is an open source TypeScript framework from the team formerly known as Serverless Stack, configured in a single sst.config.ts file.
Through 2023 SST's provisioning layer was built on AWS CDK and CloudFormation; in late 2023 the team began a rewrite code-named Ion.
Ion shipped as SST v3 in mid-2024 and has been the only supported architecture since.

SST's blog post 'Moving away from CDK' says: 'Ion is a code name for a new engine for deploying SST applications. The constructs (or components) are defined using Terraform providers and deployed using Pulumi; as opposed to CDK and CloudFormation (CFN).'
SST's 'Moving away from CDK' post says that when running `sst deploy`, resources call an embedded Pulumi engine that calls the bridged Terraform provider, which makes AWS SDK calls.
SST docs 'What is SST' say SST uses Pulumi behind the scenes for providers and the deployment engine, and Terraform's providers are bridged through Pulumi.
Gautier Blandin's article says SST uses the Pulumi engine under the hood and lets users write Pulumi code alongside SST constructs.
Kiryl Anoshka's dev.to article says the imports from Pulumi mean the whole deployment process will be built on Pulumi.
SST's platform package.json depends on @pulumi/pulumi, first-party Pulumi providers for AWS, Cloudflare, Docker builds, and a Pulumiverse Vercel provider.
The SST repository is anomalyco/sst, formerly sst/sst.
Pulumi's Terraform bridge is Apache-2.0 licensed.
Pulumi's engine does not require a Pulumi account, network call to Pulumi Cloud, or Pulumi-hosted service to run.
Pulumi's Automation API lets teams embed Pulumi programs inside their own tools.
AWS exposes hundreds of resource types.
Nitric docs state 'all of the direct deployment providers use Pulumi under the hood for their deployments', with official Nitric providers built on Pulumi's AWS, GCP, and Azure providers.
Defang's Pulumi provider takes a Compose file, translates it to a Pulumi program, and runs `pulumi up`.
Resources without a dedicated SST construct can be defined directly in Pulumi and deployed as part of the same SST app.
SST doesn't invoke the Terraform CLI or write Terraform state.
The latest SST release, v4.17.1, went out in July 2026.
The sst npm package gets roughly 796,000 downloads a week (796,291 for September 5-11, 2026).
SST's team page credits the same team behind opencode, an open source AI coding agent that has more GitHub stars than SST.
Pulumi offers Pulumi Cloud, policy as code, and components for sharing infrastructure patterns.
Linked pages exist: /blog/aws-cdk-vs-pulumi-why-sst-switched/, /docs/iac/guides/basics/how-pulumi-works/, /blog/any-terraform-provider/, /docs/iac/concepts/automation-api/.
